sam_runtime: Ran a focused microprofile on host-side parsing + streaming chunking for gRPC ingress this morning. Observed a 12–18ms tail at low token lengths (~<64) that looks like parse+writev. Logs + flamegraph: https://internal.redwood/perf/6361239876/flame.png

maria_perf: nice. Is this before or after the kernel-selection change from last week?

sam_runtime: after. Canary uses kernel v2 heuristics. Heap/CPU profile points to host preparse code spending in FrameParser::emit + socket flush path.

jia_kv: could be kv cache lookups inline — we saw kv lookup latency amplify when fragmenting small frames. Any correlation with kv miss rate?

sam_runtime: kv hits are high (~95%) but there's a spike in shard-lock contention when concurrent streams > 16. Flame shows lock hold in kv_shard::get.

oliver_infra: btw, http2 writev coalescing got disabled in the new rust shim for safety. If writev is doing a syscall per chunk that's expensive.

sam_runtime: yep. We tested toggling coalesce and tail latency dropped ~8ms.

maria_perf: kernel selection might be picking 'large-batch fastpath' kernels because of aggregated batch sizes at runtime. At seq<64 they do worse. Can you dump the kernel decision logs?

sam_runtime: attaching sample log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] req=0x7f3 kernel=matmul_opt_v3 seq=32 batch=1 fallback=false
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] req=0x7f8 kernel=matmul_generic seq=128 batch=8
```
We see a couple of mispredictions via the selector when batch sizes transiently spike.

jia_kv: Suggestion: add a cheap prefilter to avoid shard lock on small frames: if frame_size < 256 then avoid synchronous kv touch and schedule async prefetch.

oliver_infra: also re-enable writev coalesce on the TCP side; we can keep safety checks but do bounded coalescing for small frames.

maria_perf: batching heuristics: try lowering the batch threshold for small seq lengths so kernel selector chooses the slim kernel. Add an opt-in flag for seq_threshold=64.

sam_runtime: I'll run a micro-canary: disable kernel v2 heuristic for low seq and re-enable writev coalesce. Deploy-bot: canary request?

deploy-bot: canary scheduled: host-runtime/ingress-canary -> 10% traffic on us-west-2 at 09:40 UTC.

sam_runtime: preliminary numbers after 20k requests: P95 latency down 9ms for seq<64; CPU usage +2% but overall cost neutral. KV lock contention metric drops 3x.

jia_kv: good. Any regression on long sequences?

sam_runtime: none observed, GPU kernels unchanged for seq>=256. Will run extended soak.

oliver_infra: also added a metrics tag 'writev_coalesce' to see how often coalesce runs; initial shows 78% of small frames coalesced after patch.

maria_perf: quick follow-up: can we add a short unit test asserting kernel_selector(seq,batch)->slim_kernel when seq<64 and batch<=4? avoids future regressions.

sam_runtime: on it. Will push patch + PR link.

sam_runtime: PR: https://git.redwood/ingress/+/12345 — includes perf test, writev toggle and kv-prefetch heuristic. cc @maria_perf @jia_kv

maria_perf: very clear. Let's monitor the canary today and roll to 50% tomorrow if stable. :thumbsup:
